message.content:
There are 26 red cards and 26 black cards in a standard deck.

Total ways to choose 3 cards:

\[
\binom{52}{3}
\]

The opposite event is that all 3 cards are the same color: all red or all black.

Number of ways to choose 3 red cards:

\[
\binom{26}{3}
\]

Number of ways to choose 3 black cards:

\[
\binom{26}{3}
\]

So the number of ways to choose 3 cards all the same color is:

\[
2\binom{26}{3}
\]

Thus,

\[
P(\text{all same color})=\frac{2\binom{26}{3}}{\binom{52}{3}}
\]

Compute:

\[
\binom{26}{3}=\frac{26\cdot25\cdot24}{6}=2600
\]

\[
\binom{52}{3}=\frac{52\cdot51\cdot50}{6}=22100
\]

So,

\[
P(\text{all same color})=\frac{2\cdot2600}{22100}=\frac{5200}{22100}=\frac{4}{17}
\]

Therefore,

\[
P(\text{not all same color})=1-\frac{4}{17}=\frac{13}{17}
\]

The answer is \(\frac{13}{17}\).
